contradictions.claimA: The invading army numbered ninety-four thousand (as rendered in the Indonesian text)
contradictions.resolution: The stated total is smaller than the 240,000 the same sentence says were destroyed, so it cannot stand.
contradictions.treatment: Adopted 940,000. Recorded in F-EMP-010 as INFERRED_RECONCILED. See AMB-001.

contradictions.claimA: No prisoners were taken; all were killed in action
contradictions.claimB: Captured imperial forces were returned to the Empire
contradictions.resolution: Not a true contradiction once scoped: the zero applies to the Jura surface phase, the prisoners to later phases.
contradictions.treatment: CAS-008 scoped to the surface phase; CAS-014 records later-phase prisoners as UNKNOWN. See AMB-012.

contradictions.claimA: Shion and others are killed in the sealed space
contradictions.resolution: The corpus establishes revival mechanics elsewhere but does not explicitly narrate her restoration.
contradictions.treatment: Both recorded. CAS-013 keeps the death with count UNKNOWN; ACT-011 status reads KILLED, LATER PRESENT AT SUMMIT. No revival event is invented.

contradictions.claimA: A force of one hundred thirteen thousand could be sent on the emperor's order
contradictions.claimB: The legions described immediately before total far more than 113,000
contradictions.resolution: Internally inconsistent within a single passage. Possibly 1,130,000 mis-rendered, or a first-wave echelon.
contradictions.treatment: Excluded from the force database. Recorded here and in AMB-002 only.

contradictions.description: Total imperial strength implied by the 70 percent figure
contradictions.claimA: The 700,000 entering the forest is about seventy percent of the whole imperial strength, implying roughly 1,000,000 total
contradictions.claimB: The Empire can mobilise more than two million including garrisons
contradictions.resolution: Reconcilable: the 70 percent is measured against deployable field strength (about one million), not the full mobilisable pool.
contradictions.treatment: Both retained. F-EMP-001 deployable ceiling of about 1,000,000 is treated as the denominator for the 70 percent.

contradictions.description: When the Dwargon eastern blockade begins
contradictions.claimA: Gazel reports the eastern gate already blockaded, before first contact
contradictions.claimB: The blockade camp scene is narrated in V14, after the Jura campaign
contradictions.resolution: Not contradictory: the blockade begins before first contact and persists; V14 narrates a later moment in the same siege.
contradictions.treatment: Blockade start placed at EVT-0016 (D-6); the camp scene remains at EVT-0319. F-EMP-031 spans both.

contradictions.description: What the 'month' and 'twenty-nine day' anchors are measured from
contradictions.claimA: A month has passed since the subordinates' gathering met (V13 Ch1 opening line)
contradictions.claimB: The chariot force was expected in about twenty-nine days or more, but the invasion was slower than expected
contradictions.resolution: Both are measured from the same reference point - the subordinates' gathering at which the corps order of battle was fixed (EVT-0004) - not from the invasion launch. Revision 3 measured them from the advance and produced an 8-day 'month' and a 28-day interval to a contact the source says took longer than 29 days.
contradictions.treatment: Re-anchored. EVT-0004 = D-38. EVT-0012 (month mark) = D-8, exactly R+30. First contact = R+38, satisfying 'slower than about twenty-nine days'. See AMB-016.

ambiguities.subject: Total size of the invasion army
ambiguities.ambiguity: The Indonesian text of V13 Ch3 renders the invading army as 'ninety-four thousand', which is smaller than the 240,000 it says were destroyed in the same sentence. Readings: (a) 940,000; (b) a corrupted number; (c) 94,000 with a separate error in the loss figure.
ambiguities.possibleOrder: The Indonesian text of V13 Ch3 renders the invading army as 'ninety-four thousand', which is smaller than the 240,000 it says were destroyed in the same sentence. Readings: (a) 940,000; (b) a corrupted number; (c) 94,000 with a separate error in the loss figure.
ambiguities.chosenPlacement: Adopted 940,000. It is internally consistent with the component figures 700,000 + 200,000 + 40,000 = 940,000 given elsewhere in V12 Ch4 and V13.

ambiguities.subject: The figure 'one hundred thirteen thousand' in V12 Ch4
ambiguities.ambiguity: V12 Ch4 says a force of 'one hundred thirteen thousand' could be sent once the emperor gave the order, immediately after describing legions totalling far more. Readings: (a) 1,130,000 mis-rendered; (b) a first-wave echelon; (c) translation corruption.
ambiguities.possibleOrder: V12 Ch4 says a force of 'one hundred thirteen thousand' could be sent once the emperor gave the order, immediately after describing legions totalling far more. Readings: (a) 1,130,000 mis-rendered; (b) a first-wave echelon; (c) translation corruption.
ambiguities.chosenPlacement: Excluded from the force database rather than guessed at. Recorded here only.

ambiguities.subject: Clock times across the whole campaign
ambiguities.ambiguity: The corpus contains essentially no clock times. Only relative durations appear (under six seconds, ten minutes, less than an hour, three hours).
ambiguities.possibleOrder: The corpus contains essentially no clock times. Only relative durations appear (under six seconds, ten minutes, less than an hour, three hours).
ambiguities.chosenPlacement: All hour-and-minute placements are SIMULATION_RECONSTRUCTED. Only the relative durations are carried as EXPLICIT_RELATIVE.

ambiguities.subject: Calendar dates
ambiguities.ambiguity: No in-world calendar date is given for any campaign event.
ambiguities.possibleOrder: No in-world calendar date is given for any campaign event.
ambiguities.chosenPlacement: Artificial marker year 9001 used. DATE_BASIS = SIMULATION_RECONSTRUCTED throughout.

ambiguities.subject: Duration of the labyrinth phase
ambiguities.ambiguity: The corpus establishes sequence and a three-hour revival cycle but never states how many days the labyrinth battle lasted.
ambiguities.possibleOrder: The corpus establishes sequence and a three-hour revival cycle but never states how many days the labyrinth battle lasted.
ambiguities.chosenPlacement: Modelled as three days (D+1 to D+3) to accommodate the multi-wave structure and the revival cycle. Purely reconstructive.

ambiguities.subject: Strength of Shion's undocumented unit
ambiguities.ambiguity: The corpus explicitly says the number of people is unknown, with a personal assessment of not more than a thousand.
ambiguities.possibleOrder: The corpus explicitly says the number of people is unknown, with a personal assessment of not more than a thousand.
ambiguities.chosenPlacement: Kept as MAX = 1,000 with no best estimate. Not counted in any total.

ambiguities.subject: V15 Chapters 4 and 5 internal structure
ambiguities.ambiguity: Eight Gates and The Truth of the Emperor concern the nature of the imperial throne and skill-level conflict rather than force-on-force battle. Little of it maps onto conventional battlefield state.
ambiguities.possibleOrder: Eight Gates and The Truth of the Emperor concern the nature of the imperial throne and skill-level conflict rather than force-on-force battle. Little of it maps onto conventional battlefield state.
ambiguities.chosenPlacement: Recorded as chapter-level events at MEDIUM/LOW confidence. Further atomic breakdown would require modelling non-military developments.

ambiguities.subject: Destination of the Warcraft Legion after the space-time jump
ambiguities.ambiguity: Velgrynd opens a space-time connection to move the flotilla; the destination is not stated in the extracted passage.
ambiguities.possibleOrder: Velgrynd opens a space-time connection to move the flotilla; the destination is not stated in the extracted passage.
ambiguities.chosenPlacement: MOV-015 records the jump with destination UNKNOWN. No route or arrival point is inferred.

ambiguities.subject: Tempest casualties in the sealed space
ambiguities.ambiguity: Shion 'and others' are killed; no count is given. Shion appears alive at the V16 summit.
ambiguities.possibleOrder: Shion 'and others' are killed; no count is given. Shion appears alive at the V16 summit.
ambiguities.chosenPlacement: Recorded as minimum one, best estimate UNKNOWN. Not converted to a number, and not offset against the later appearance.

ambiguities.subject: Whether the 60,000 ritual sacrifice is part of the 940,000
ambiguities.ambiguity: The Hybrid Legion is a separate legion from the Jura invasion force in V12 Ch4, and the 60,000 blockade the eastern metropolis rather than the Jura front.
ambiguities.possibleOrder: The Hybrid Legion is a separate legion from the Jura invasion force in V12 Ch4, and the 60,000 blockade the eastern metropolis rather than the Jura front.
ambiguities.chosenPlacement: Treated as SEPARATE from the 940,000. Campaign totals report the two figures distinctly.

ambiguities.subject: Number of imperial prisoners repatriated
ambiguities.ambiguity: V16 Ch3 confirms captured imperial forces were returned but gives no figure. This differs in kind, not in fact, from the surface phase where no prisoners were taken.
ambiguities.possibleOrder: V16 Ch3 confirms captured imperial forces were returned but gives no figure. This differs in kind, not in fact, from the surface phase where no prisoners were taken.
ambiguities.chosenPlacement: CAS-008 scoped explicitly to the surface phase; CAS-014 records later-phase prisoners as UNKNOWN.

ambiguities.subject: V16 scope boundary
ambiguities.ambiguity: Most of V16 concerns the Feldway and Michael conflict, which is a separate later war rather than part of the Tempest-Eastern Empire War.
ambiguities.possibleOrder: Most of V16 concerns the Feldway and Michael conflict, which is a separate later war rather than part of the Tempest-Eastern Empire War.
ambiguities.chosenPlacement: Only V16 Ch3 (post-war settlement and rebuilding) is extracted. The later conflict is deliberately excluded per scope.

ambiguities.subject: Interval between the Jura campaign and the second phase
ambiguities.ambiguity: The corpus places the second phase 'several days' after the Jura campaign but gives no figure. Revision 3 joined them same-day, which is not 'several days'.
ambiguities.possibleOrder: The corpus places the second phase 'several days' after the Jura campaign but gives no figure. Revision 3 joined them same-day, which is not 'several days'.
ambiguities.chosenPlacement: Widened to a 3-day gap: EVT-0207 at D+3, EVT-0310 at D+6. Three days is the minimum defensible reading of 'several'. The gap itself is SIMULATION_RECONSTRUCTED and remains the weakest join in the dataset.

ambiguities.subject: Distribution of the approach march across the interval
ambiguities.ambiguity: The corpus fixes the start of the advance, a ~29-day forecast that was overshot, an explicit month mark, a border crossing, a halt-and-deploy and forest entry - but no intermediate positions, distances or dates.
ambiguities.possibleOrder: The corpus fixes the start of the advance, a ~29-day forecast that was overshot, an explicit month mark, a border crossing, a halt-and-deploy and forest entry - but no intermediate positions, distances or dates.
ambiguities.chosenPlacement: Approach events spread across D-37 to D-1 by simulation placement. Column position is exposed as Approach_Progress_Pct, a linear interpolation between two source-supported endpoints. The percentage is NOT a measured distance and no distance is claimed.

ambiguities.subject: Interval between mobilization and the subordinates' gathering
ambiguities.ambiguity: The corpus gives no interval between the imperial mobilization order (V12 Ch4) and the subordinates' gathering (V12 Ch2) that serves as the temporal reference point.
ambiguities.possibleOrder: The corpus gives no interval between the imperial mobilization order (V12 Ch4) and the subordinates' gathering (V12 Ch2) that serves as the temporal reference point.
ambiguities.chosenPlacement: Set to 2 days (D-40 to D-38) by simulation placement. Nothing in the corpus constrains it; the campaign window would shift with any other reading.

ambiguities.subject: What the reference point for the month and 29-day anchors actually is
ambiguities.ambiguity: V13 Ch1 opens 'a month has passed since the subordinates' gathering met'. Candidate referents: (a) the V12 Ch2 meeting at which the corps order of battle was fixed; (b) a separate unnarrated gathering; (c) a translation artefact for a different assembly.
ambiguities.possibleOrder: V13 Ch1 opens 'a month has passed since the subordinates' gathering met'. Candidate referents: (a) the V12 Ch2 meeting at which the corps order of battle was fixed; (b) a separate unnarrated gathering; (c) a translation artefact for a different assembly.
ambiguities.chosenPlacement: Reading (a) adopted: it is the only gathering of Rimuru's subordinates the corpus narrates in the relevant window, and it makes both surviving duration anchors mutually consistent. Recorded as REFERENCE_EVENT = EVT-0004 at D-38. If (b) or (c) were correct the whole approach window would shift, though its internal order would not.

ambiguities.subject: The 50-day campaign window is a simulation window, not a canonical duration
ambiguities.ambiguity: No passage states how long the war lasted. The window is assembled from: mobilization to gathering (unconstrained, AMB-015), gathering to contact (R+38, constrained by two anchors), contact to labyrinth conclusion (D+0 to D+3, AMB-005), the 'several days' gap (AMB-006), and the second phase and settlement (sequence only).
ambiguities.possibleOrder: No passage states how long the war lasted. The window is assembled from: mobilization to gathering (unconstrained, AMB-015), gathering to contact (R+38, constrained by two anchors), contact to labyrinth conclusion (D+0 to D+3, AMB-005), the 'several days' gap (AMB-006), and the second phase and settlement (sequence only).
ambiguities.chosenPlacement: 50 days is the SIMULATION CAMPAIGN WINDOW. It must never be quoted as a canonical war duration.
